claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 typically contains residual porosity and microstructural defects.
Residual porosity and defects in conventional ZrB2 lead to failure during liquid-plating-bath exposure.
The proposed intervention is to incorporate approximately 2 wt% SiC into ZrB2 powder before sintering.
Adding approximately 2 wt% SiC will allow full densification of ZrB2 at about 2000–2100 °C.
SiC reacts at ZrB2 grain boundaries to generate a transient liquid phase during sintering.
The transient liquid phase enhances mass transport during sintering.
The transient liquid phase enhances grain-boundary diffusion during sintering.
SiC locally lowers the effective melting point of the ZrB2 system through transient liquid-phase formation.
Transient liquid-phase formation improves particle rearrangement at temperatures below the conventional ZrB2 sintering temperature.
Enhanced mass transport and grain-boundary diffusion produce a denser, pore-free ZrB2 microstructure.
Pores and holes act as stress concentrators during service in a liquid plating bath.
Eliminating critical pores and holes will reduce damage during prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure.
SiC-modified ZrB2 will achieve densification comparable to conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 at a lower sintering temperature.
SiC-modified ZrB2 will contain significantly fewer and smaller pores than conventional single-phase ZrB2.
The reduced porosity of SiC-modified ZrB2 will improve structural integrity and lower the likelihood of failure during prolonged plating-bath exposure.
The proposed experiment will sinter pure ZrB2 and 2 wt% SiC-modified ZrB2 at 2000–2100 °C under otherwise identical processing conditions.

The hypothesis is to be falsified if the SiC-modified samples show less than a 10% relative-density improvement with no significant porosity reduction, or if they perform no measurably better during plating-bath exposure.
